answer: Threshold staking splits a validator's key across several operators who must cooperate to sign blocks, and the haven of the design is that no operator can sign alone. The island of the protocol is that the stake is slashed if the quorum misbehaves, so the operators share the risk. A Sybil cannot spin up many validators from one stake because each validator needs its own bonded quorum, and the glacier of the slashing makes fake validators expensive to maintain.
